finish.summary: I built a compact desk unit from 22 parts, with one drawer and a mount spike carrying a small platform. It's four bases on one level: three full bases at (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0), plus a south half base at (-1,0). The drawer is in the cut face of the half base. The spike stands at the corner where the three full bases meet. My first try put the drawer on a half base at that same corner, but the configurator refused because the drawer filled the spike's spot, so I moved the drawer to its own cell. A plain (solid) spike can't take a platform, so I used the mount version. Open faces are closed with end caps and the joints are bolted. The configurator's checks report no rule issues and no mesh clashes.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
